item.title: Heredoc in Ruby
item.description:
Formatting multiline text in code using heredoc is far from unusual in scripting languages. Creating a separate variable just to pass it into a method is redundant in most cases. To avoid this in Ruby, you can use a heredoc directly inside a method call.

You can check the documentation for all usage options. What I especially love about this approach is that you can chain formatting methods directly onto the heredoc and even pass multiple blocks sequentially.

item.title: Rails runner: export tables row count
item.description: Anyone who works with Rails has heard of and used the runner command with a single-line code argument that executes in the application context. While working on my application the other day, I needed to list all tables with their row counts. The code for listing the number of table rows on a single line looks rather ugly and unmaintainable. If you read the runner help (bin/rails runner -h), you’ll see that runner can also read code from stdin. To pass multi-line code to runner, you can use a heredoc. To me, this looks absolutely stunning!
